title: a `neural_block` descriptor with scalar_type=softdouble is rejected — the neural check is stricter than the general dtype check
why: The neural wire format only supports native float32/float64: SoftDouble is
a GPU code-generation numeric type, not an array dtype, and is not part of
`softdouble` is a perfectly valid `scalar_type` for an ordinary sidecar (the
existing float64 wire representation already serves it bit-identically), so
this fixture passes the shared validator's general dtype check and is
rejected only by the neural-specific check, which allows just
{float32, float64} rather than merely disallowing SoftDouble. The
companion row10b fixture proves the reverse: the same scalar_type is
accepted once the pattern is not `neural_block`, showing the rejection is
scoped to the neural pattern, not global.
The manifest-bypassing plugin loader is exercised too, since its only
structural gate is the shared validator.
